action: Inventory internet-facing apps and restrict admin, hypervisor and backup interfaces to private networks. Review ConnectWise-related Microsoft 365 app activity from October 1, 2026, rate-limit high-impact APIs, and rotate exposed secrets.
exec: Automated intrusions completing in hours shorten the time defenders have to detect and respond.
plain: The FBI warns that attackers are using ARTEX, a free AI-driven hacking tool, to break into organisations with little human effort, sometimes gaining high-level access in under three hours.

key_findings: Organisations worldwide in finance, government, technology, defence, semiconductors, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, telecoms and legal services are affected.
ARTEX turns plain-language goals into commands run by AI agents and relies on external LLM providers; attacker instances mostly use Chinese-origin models.
Some intrusions reached privileged access in under three hours; researchers counted over 1,600 exposed ARTEX consoles in early November 2026.
Entry came through ordinary web flaws (unsigned SAML assertions, injection, missing API authentication), weak or hardcoded admin credentials, stolen VPN configs and partner-tenant trust abuse.
A ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise led to attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 downstream tenants; a South Korean financial campaign took data on about 67,000 people.
recommendations: Inventory all internet-facing applications, including legacy and peripheral systems.
Restrict admin, SCM/Kudu, hypervisor and backup interfaces to trusted or private networks.
Apply least privilege to multi-tenant app permissions and monitor credential additions and high-privilege app-only activity.
Review ConnectWise-related activity from October 1, 2026 and keep affected connections disabled until ConnectWise issues restoration instructions.
Preserve Entra sign-in and audit logs before removing unauthorised credentials or grants.

summary: FBI FLASH-20261113-001 (TLP:CLEAR) says threat actors have used the open-source, LLM-driven ARTEX agent platform since at least August 2026 to automate intrusions from reconnaissance to data theft. Some reached privileged access in under three hours. It cites a South Korean financial campaign exposing about 67,000 people and a ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise with attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 downstream tenants.
title: FBI FLASH: ARTEX autonomous penetration-testing framework used to automate intrusions

validation.note: Reviewed against the original FBI document.
